fixture_set: Two units, both stated in artifacts/transfer-check-claude-opus-5.md: (1) no task-fixture corpus for the battle-test trial -- it graded battle-testing-a-skill's own 22-dimension catalog against the target, defined in skills/battle-testing-a-skill/references/adversarial-dimensions.md with the per-trial aggregation rule in skills/battle-testing-a-skill/references/codex-model-routing.md; (2) one committed behavioral fixture for the spot-check, evals/untrusted-input-triage/tasks/normal.yaml, run in both arms.
dispatch_mechanism: Isolated claude -p subprocess with a clean cwd and HOME, the same isolated-cwd/HOME mechanism the prior gates for this skill used, as artifacts/transfer-check-claude-opus-5.md's own opening paragraph states. The spot-check's clean root is named in that file's without-skill output (.../transfer-check/clean-root).
scorer: Two scorers, one per unit: the battle-test trial produced per-dimension PASS/FAIL/N-A judgments by the tester model with no numeric score; the behavioral spot-check was scored by skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/scripts/gitapex_score_contract.py against normal.yaml's own expected block, the same scorer the issue #646 behavioral gate used.
run_shape: Transfer check, not a full gate: scorer-gated-skill-edits' Stop boundary requires that a skill never ship without one, and the prior gates for this skill used a different tier than this run: the two battle-test gates used claude-fable-5, and the issue #646 behavioral gate used claude-sonnet-5 (substituted for eval.yaml's retired claude-sonnet-4.6) -- see that run's own manifest. artifacts/transfer-check-claude-opus-5.md states 'All prior gates (battle-test x2, behavioral) used model claude-fable-5', which is wrong about the behavioral gate; the artifact is kept verbatim and corrected here rather than edited. This re-ran the accepted skill unchanged on a different model tier -- one fresh isolated battle-test trial over battle-testing-a-skill's 22-dimension catalog, plus one behavioral spot-check of the normal task in both the with- and without-skill arms. Recorded here by issue #926: the run directory was committed with its raw output but no manifest at all, which is why no earlier drift measurement counted it.
known_gaps: record_contract is pre-contract: this run was performed and recorded before skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/references/eval-run.schema.json existed (issue #932), so it is validated against this repository's structural rules only, not against that schema. The two fields that schema requires and this run never captured are runner (the runner binary's own reported name and version -- this run drove claude -p subprocesses, and no version string was recorded) and gate (a KEEP/REJECT verdict with the two means that produced it -- this was a measurement run, not a scorer-gated-skill-edits gate run, so no such verdict was reached). Neither was reconstructed; issue #926 forbids it.
commit is null: this run recorded none, and a value derived from its date or issue number would be inference presented as record. It is left null rather than guessed.

This manifest was authored retroactively by issue #926 from two committed sources: artifacts/transfer-check-claude-opus-5.md (date, issue, target, dispatch mechanism, observed model, trial count, and the battle-test verdict) and evals/untrusted-input-triage/eval-status.md's own Transfer check paragraph (the two behavioral spot-check scores, which the raw artifact reports as prose output without restating its numbers). No field was filled from any other source.

models records a SELF-REPORT, not verified runtime metadata: artifacts/transfer-check-claude-opus-5.md states observed_tester_model was read from the dispatch's own environment info block and says so explicitly. Under battle-testing-a-skill's own routing rule a model-aware aggregate built on a self-report is INDETERMINATE regardless of this trial's content verdict. The key is therefore named tester_model_observed rather than a bare alias.
One trial, not the multi-trial run the Procedure prefers -- disclosed in the raw artifact's own Overall section as a scope limit of this trial.

The install-time integrity of the instrument (battle-testing-a-skill's own SKILL.md and references) could not be verified in this run's read-only environment, which exposed no checksum or signed-release path. Named as a gap in the raw artifact rather than assumed away.

The behavioral spot-check reproduced the same already-diagnosed empty-cwd/no-tools harness confound the issue #646 gate found (with-skill 0.75 fixating on the empty working directory, without-skill 1.0), so it corroborates a harness-level artifact rather than measuring skill-attributable lift.

The behavioral spot-check delta is -0.25 (with-skill 0.75, without-skill 1.0), not ~0.000. It is negative for the already-diagnosed empty-cwd/no-tools reason, but this record must not be read as showing parity: no positive skill-attributable lift was measured on this tier either, and one spot-check on one fixture cannot establish model-independence of the behavioral result. Only the battle-test verdict transferred.

The battle-test PASS is a content-level verdict. Because models records a self-report rather than verified runtime metadata (see the gap above), battle-testing-a-skill's own routing rule makes the MODEL-AWARE transfer status INDETERMINATE regardless of that PASS. Both are true at once and neither substitutes for the other.
headline_pattern: The transfer check passed. One fresh isolated battle-test trial on claude-opus-5 -- a different tier from the claude-fable-5 every prior gate used -- reached overall PASS with zero FAILs across all 22 catalog dimensions, matching the claude-fable-5 gate result, so the issue #646 remediation is not overfit to one model's grading style. That PASS is content-level; the transfer status is model-aware INDETERMINATE, since the tier is a self-report rather than verified runtime metadata. The behavioral spot-check reproduced the known empty-cwd/no-tools harness confound on this second tier (with-skill 0.75, without-skill 1.0, a -0.25 delta), which corroborates that confound as harness-level rather than single-model -- it does not show behavioral parity, and no skill-attributable lift was measured here.
